english.title: Assault an immigration officer - UK Borders Act 2007
english.standardoffencewording: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) assaulted an immigration officer, namely **(..SPECIFY THE PERSON..)
english.legislation: Contrary to section 22 of the UK Borders Act 2007.
english.pointstoprove:
date and location
assaulted an immigration officer

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) Section 22(5) of the UK Border Act 2007 provides that in relation to an offence committed before the commencement of section 281(5) of the Criminal Justice Act 2003 references in section 22(2)(a) of the Act to 51 weeks shall be treated as a reference to six months.
(ii) Section 23(2) of the UK Border Act 2007 provides that an offence under section 22 shall be treated as-
(a) a relevant offence for the purposes of sections 28B and 28D of the Immigration Act 1971 (search, entry and arrest), and (b) an offence under Part 3 of that Act (criminal proceedings) for the purposes of sections 28(4), 28E, 28G and 28H (search after arrest, andc.) of that Act.
(iii) Section 23(3) of the UK Border Act 2007 provides that the following provisions of the Immigration Act 1971 shall have effect in connection with an offence under section 22 of this Act as they have effect in connection with an offence under that Act-
(a) section 28I (seized material: access and copying),
(b) section 28J (search warrants: safeguards),
(c) section 28K (execution of warrants), and
(d) section 28L(1) (interpretation).

other.powersofarrest:
arrest without warrant

Section 23(1) of the UK Borders Act 2007 provides that an immigration officer may arrest a person without warrant if the officer reasonably suspects that the person has committed or is about to commit an offence under section 22.
other.penalty:
Summary: Imprisonment for a term not exceeding 51 weeks and/or a fine not exceeding level 5 on the standard scale.

Note:
Until the commencement of section 281(5) of the Criminal Justice Act 2003 - 51 weeks imprisonment shall be treated as a reference to six months imprisonment. (Section 3(5)).

Time limit on prosecutions:
6 months

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
